title: annak ellenére, hogy: Despite the Fact That

sections.title: Introducing a contrast inside one sentence
sections.content: *annak ellenére, hogy* introduces a concession: something is true or happens even though another, seemingly contradictory thing is also true. It's built from *ellenére*, a postposition meaning "despite/in spite of" that governs the dative case, plus *annak* — the dative form of *az* ("that") — pointing forward to the *hogy*-clause that explains what "that" is. The whole unit works like a fixed frame: *Annak ellenére, hogy* [clause with a normal conjugated verb], [main clause].

sections.title: Word order: both positions work
rows: Annak ellenére, hogy sokat veszekedünk, mindig kibékülünk.
Despite the fact that we argue a lot, we always make up.
Mindig kibékülünk, annak ellenére, hogy sokat veszekedünk.
We always make up, despite the fact that we argue a lot.

items.spanish: Annak ellenére, hogy nagyon különbözőek vagyunk, jól kijövünk egymással.
items.english: Despite the fact that we're very different, we get along well with each other.

items.spanish: Még mindig barátok vagyunk, annak ellenére, hogy évek óta nem találkoztunk.
items.english: We're still friends, despite the fact that we haven't met in years.

items.spanish: Annak ellenére, hogy megbántott, megbocsátottam neki.
items.english: Despite the fact that he/she hurt me, I forgave him/her.

sections.content: The *hogy*-clause always has its own fully conjugated verb — *annak ellenére, hogy sokat veszekedünk*, never a shortened infinitive form. Keep *annak* in place even though English "despite the fact that" doesn't translate it word for word; dropping it (just *ellenére, hogy*...) is a common learner mistake and sounds unfinished in Hungarian.
